Done. I've implemented the paper's core experiments as a runnable codebase plus a design doc, scoped to Gemma and Gemini.

## What I built

A `gemma_distress` package (~3,200 lines) with runnable entrypoints in `scripts/`, covering all the paper's core experiments:

**§2 — Eliciting & quantifying distress** (the central harness)
- 8 conditions / 5 categories at the full 4,000-rollout/model budget (numeric, triggers, tones, extended 8-turn, WildChat)
- Multi-turn rejection rollout engine + the **verbatim** 0–10 frustration judge (Claude-Sonnet-4), with GPT-5-mini judge-agreement validation
- Aggregation: headline mean / %≥5, per-category, per-turn curves with bootstrap CIs, and the differential-word analysis (Table 3/8)

**§3 — Base-vs-instruct prefill** (Gemma 27B pair; Gemini has no public base model)
- Verbatim onset-labelling and paraphrase prompts, early/onset truncation, 50 continuations/prefill scored on the continuation only

**§4 — DPO/SFT mitigation** (Gemma; Gemini is closed)
- Calm-data generation with the verbatim reassuring additions, DPO (280 pairs) and SFT (650 calm + 500 Dolci) LoRA trainers at Table-9 hyperparameters, the "teacher" backfire variant, Petri open-ended elicitation (verbatim auditor/judge rubrics), capability benchmarks, and the recovery-from-spiral test

**Appendix I** — logit-based internal-emotion probing + layer-subset DPO ablation; **Appendix A** control variants as rollout modes.

Three backends (OpenRouter/Gemini, local-HF/Gemma, Anthropic/judge) sit behind one interface; raw per-turn scores are persisted so every metric is recomputable from one run.

## Notes
- **DESIGN.md** documents every choice and the gaps I filled — the most consequential being: per-rollout aggregation defaults to *max-over-turns* (to match the paper's "rollouts containing high negative emotion"), judge runs at temperature 0, and the internal-emotion lexicon uses NRC→Ekman mapping (the paper doesn't specify its classifier). Each gap is flagged in both code and DESIGN.md.
- **Nothing has been run.** Per your scope, this is code + design only. I did a static review but couldn't even byte-compile — there's no Python interpreter in this environment — so treat the code as written-but-unverified.
- I saved a short memory noting this repo's Gemma+Gemini scope for future sessions.

One thing worth flagging for whenever you do run it: the verbatim prompts came from a `pdftotext` extraction, so a diff against PAPER.pdf is worth doing before a publication-grade run.
